chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:

Indeed, I feel mercy for three people, and it is their right to be shown mercy: a noble person who has been struck by humiliation after honor, a wealthy person who has been struck by need after affluence, and a scholar whom his own people and the ignorant treat lightly.

key_terms.الْجَهَلَةُ: The ignorant people who fail to recognize true worth
key_terms.حَاجَةٌ: Need, want, or poverty after prior affluence
key_terms.عَالِمٌ: A scholar, one possessing sacred knowledge
key_terms.عَزِيزٌ: A person of honor, dignity, or elevated standing
key_terms.مَذَلَّةٌ: Humiliation or abasement after a state of honor

ai.seo_question: Which kinds of people are especially deserving of mercy in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches compassion for people who suffer a painful reversal in their condition or whose worth is not properly recognized. It highlights the human dignity of the honored who are humiliated, the wealthy who fall into need, and the scholar who is belittled by his people and by the ignorant.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5837 - Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), said:

"Indeed, I feel mercy for three people, and it is their right to be shown mercy:
A noble person who has been humiliated after his honor,
A wealthy person who has fallen into poverty after wealth,
And a scholar who is belittled by his own people and the ignorant."
